title: Psalms Chapter 82 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 82 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 82 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 82.

questions.question: Who is the author of Psalms 82?
questions.explanation: The chapter begins with 'A Psalm of Asaph.' (Psalms 82:1)

questions.question: In Psalms 82, where does God stand?
options: In the congregation of the mighty
questions.correctAnswer: In the congregation of the mighty
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'God standeth in the congregation of the mighty.' (Psalms 82:1)

questions.question: What does God do among the gods according to Psalms 82:1?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that 'he judgeth among the gods.' (Psalms 82:1)

questions.question: How long does God question the unjust judgment in Psalms 82:2?
questions.explanation: The verse begins with the question, 'How long will ye judge unjustly...' (Psalms 82:2)

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 82:2 encourages the acceptance of the persons of the wicked.
questions.explanation: The verse asks how long they will 'accept the persons of the wicked,' implying it is wrong to do so. (Psalms 82:2)

questions.question: In Psalms 82:3, who are we instructed to defend?
questions.explanation: The verse specifically states, 'Defend the poor and fatherless.' (Psalms 82:3)

questions.question: What action does Psalms 82:3 call for towards the afflicted and needy?
questions.explanation: The verse commands to 'do justice to the afflicted and needy.' (Psalms 82:3)

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 82:4 encourages delivering the wealthy from their troubles.
questions.explanation: The verse speaks about delivering the poor and needy, not the wealthy. (Psalms 82:4)

questions.question: What does Psalms 82:5 say about those who know not and understand not?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'they walk on in darkness.' (Psalms 82:5)

questions.question: In Psalms 82:6, who are referred to as 'gods'?
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.' (Psalms 82:6)

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 82:7 states that the 'gods' shall live forever.
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that they shall 'die like men,' which implies they will not live forever. (Psalms 82:7)

questions.question: What does Psalms 82:8 request God to do?
questions.explanation: The verse directly states, 'Arise, O God, judge the earth.' (Psalms 82:8)

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 82:8 affirms that God will inherit all nations.
questions.explanation: The verse concludes with 'for thou shalt inherit all nations,' affirming God's authority. (Psalms 82:8)

questions.question: In Psalms 82, which instruction comes first?
options: Accept the persons of the wicked
questions.explanation: The first instruction given is to 'Defend the poor and fatherless.' (Psalms 82:3)

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 82 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 82 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Psalms 82:3 instruct us to do regarding the poor and fatherless?
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:3 instructs to 'Defend the poor and fatherless: do justice to the afflicted and needy,' emphasizing the importance of caring for those in need.

questions.question: According to Psalms 82:4, what should we do to the poor and needy?
options: Rid them out of the hand of the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: Rid them out of the hand of the wicked
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:4 says, 'Deliver the poor and needy: rid them out of the hand of the wicked,' indicating the need to protect the vulnerable from oppression.

questions.question: What does Psalms 82:5 say about those who do not understand?
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:5 states, 'They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness,' highlighting the consequences of ignorance.

questions.question: How does Psalms 82:6 describe the status of the audience addressed?
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:6 declares, 'I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High,' indicating their elevated status but also their accountability.

questions.question: What consequence is mentioned in Psalms 82:7 for those addressed in the Psalm?
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:7 states, 'But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes,' reminding the audience of their mortality despite their status.

questions.question: What does Psalms 82:8 ask God to do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:8 says, 'Arise, O God, judge the earth: for thou shalt inherit all nations,' calling for divine justice.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 82:3, we are instructed to ignore the poor and fatherless.
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:3 instructs us to 'Defend the poor and fatherless,' indicating that we should not ignore them.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 82:6 emphasizes that all people are children of the Most High.
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:6 states, 'Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High,' affirming the divine relationship.

questions.question: What does Psalms 82:5 imply about the foundations of the earth?
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:5 says, 'all the foundations of the earth are out of course,' indicating a state of disorder due to injustice.

questions.question: What does Psalms 82:4 suggest we must do to fulfill our responsibility towards the needy?
options: Deliver and rid them of wickedness
questions.correctAnswer: Deliver and rid them of wickedness
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:4 instructs to 'Deliver the poor and needy: rid them out of the hand of the wicked,' emphasizing active involvement.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 82:2 questions the fairness of judgment among the wicked.
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:2 asks, 'How long will ye judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked?' questioning the fairness of judgment.

questions.question: According to Psalms 82:3, what kind of justice should be done?
options: Justice for the afflicted and needy
questions.correctAnswer: Justice for the afflicted and needy
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:3 calls for 'do justice to the afflicted and needy,' focusing on the vulnerable rather than the powerful.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'walk on in darkness' in Psalms 82:5 imply about ignorance?
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:5 indicates that walking in darkness due to ignorance can lead to dire consequences, as 'all the foundations of the earth are out of course.'

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 82 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 82.

questions.question: Who is the author of Psalms 82?
questions.explanation: The Psalm is specifically noted as a Psalm of Asaph in Psalms 82:1.

questions.question: What does God do in the congregation of the mighty according to Psalms 82?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that God judgeth among the gods, as seen in Psalms 82:1.

questions.question: According to Psalms 82:4, what is one action that God commands?
options: To deliver the poor and needy
questions.correctAnswer: To deliver the poor and needy
questions.explanation: The verse instructs to deliver the poor and needy, as stated in Psalms 82:4.

questions.question: In Psalms 82:5, what do the people fail to understand?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that they know not and walk in darkness, causing the foundations of the earth to be out of course, as seen in Psalms 82:5.

questions.question: What profound statement does God make about the judges in Psalms 82:6?
options: They are all children of the Most High
They will be judged by men
questions.correctAnswer: They are all children of the Most High
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High', indicating their elevated status, as noted in Psalms 82:6.

questions.question: What fate is described for the judges in Psalms 82:7?
options: They will be judged by God
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states that they shall die like men, indicating their mortality despite their title, as seen in Psalms 82:7.

questions.question: According to Psalms 82:8, what does the psalmist request God to do?
questions.explanation: The psalmist calls upon God to arise and judge the earth, as stated in Psalms 82:8.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 82 emphasizes the importance of defending the poor and needy.
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:3 specifically instructs to defend the poor and fatherless and do justice to the afflicted and needy.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the concept of believers being referred to as 'gods'?
questions.explanation: In John 10:34, Jesus quotes Psalms 82:6, referring to those whom the word of God came to as 'gods'.

questions.question: What literary device is utilized in Psalms 82 through the phrase 'ye are gods'?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'ye are gods' serves as a metaphor emphasizing the elevated status of judges, reflecting a literary device used in Psalms 82:6.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 82 suggests that there is no accountability for the leaders who judge unjustly.
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:7 indicates that even those who are called 'gods' will die like men, implying accountability for their actions.

questions.question: How does the theme of justice in Psalms 82 relate to the prophetic literature, particularly in Isaiah?
options: Both emphasize the need for justice
questions.correctAnswer: Both emphasize the need for justice
questions.explanation: Both Psalms 82 and many passages in Isaiah focus on justice for the poor and oppressed, highlighting a shared theme.

questions.question: In Psalms 82:5, what is the term used to describe the state of the judges?
questions.explanation: The verse describes them as not knowing or understanding, illustrating their ignorance, as seen in Psalms 82:5.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'fall like one of the princes' in Psalms 82:7?
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that even those in high positions will face mortality and fall, as stated in Psalms 82:7.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 82 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 82 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What role does God play among the mighty according to Psalms 82?
questions.explanation: This is stated in Psalms 82:1, where it mentions that God stands in the congregation of the mighty and judges among the gods, highlighting His sovereign authority.

questions.question: In Psalms 82, what does God question about the judges?
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:2 asks, 'How long will ye judge unjustly?', indicating God's concern over the lack of justice among the judges.

questions.question: What does God instruct the judges to do in Psalms 82:3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:3 clearly states God’s directive to defend the poor and fatherless and to do justice to the afflicted and needy.

questions.question: What condition does Psalms 82:4 describe regarding the poor and needy?
options: They are rid of the wicked
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:4 urges the judges to deliver the poor and needy and rid them out of the hand of the wicked, indicating their vulnerable condition.

questions.question: What is the consequence mentioned in Psalms 82 for those who judge unjustly?
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:7 states, 'But ye shall die like men', emphasizing the mortality and ultimate accountability of unjust judges.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted in Psalms 82:1 by His act of judging?
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:1 highlights God’s justice as He judges among the gods, demonstrating His role as the ultimate judge.

questions.question: What does Psalms 82:6 suggest about the identity of the judges?
options: They are humans endowed with authority
questions.correctAnswer: They are humans endowed with authority
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:6 indicates that the judges are referred to as gods, implying their divinely appointed authority as children of the Most High.

questions.question: How does Psalms 82 connect with the overarching narrative of redemption?
options: It highlights social justice as a reflection of God's character
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights social justice as a reflection of God's character
questions.explanation: Psalms 82 calls for justice and protection for the vulnerable, connecting with the biblical theme of God’s concern for justice and redemption for the oppressed.

questions.question: What does Psalms 82:5 reveal about the understanding of the unjust judges?
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:5 describes the judges as not knowing and walking in darkness, indicating their moral and spiritual failure.

questions.question: What future hope is expressed in Psalms 82:8?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 82:8, the call for God to arise and judge the earth reflects a future hope for divine justice and restoration.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 3 and 4 convey about God's expectations for leaders?
options: They should protect and deliver the vulnerable
questions.correctAnswer: They should protect and deliver the vulnerable
questions.explanation: Verses 3 and 4 together emphasize God’s expectation for leaders to defend the poor and needy and deliver them from wickedness.

questions.question: What do verses 6 and 7 together reveal about the fate of unjust judges?
options: They will be rewarded in heaven
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 together illustrate the contrast between the judges' divine status and their mortality, emphasizing their accountability.

questions.question: What does Psalms 82:2 imply about the nature of justice?
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:2's questioning of unjust judgments underlines the expectation that justice should be impartial and not accept the persons of the wicked.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not care about social justice. What does Psalms 82:3-4 actually teach?
options: God only cares about personal piety
God commands justice for the marginalized
God is indifferent to human suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God commands justice for the marginalized
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:3-4 teaches that God commands the protection and justice for the poor and fatherless, directly countering the sceptics' claim.

questions.question: How does the imagery of 'walking in darkness' in Psalms 82:5 relate to spiritual blindness?
options: It demonstrates knowledge of God's will
questions.explanation: Psalms 82:5's imagery of 'walking in darkness' signifies a lack of understanding and awareness of their responsibilities in upholding justice.
